usdRate.sourceName: BCRA wholesale reference exchange rate (Communication A 3500), series 5
usdRate.note: Pesos per US dollar, official wholesale reference rate; World Bank PA.NUS.FCRF gives a 2025 average of 1,240.85.

inflation_cpi.sourceName: INDEC consumer price index (national), as published in BCRA statistics series 28
inflation_cpi.note: Year-on-year CPI inflation 33.4% in September 2026 (1.9% in the month); 31.5% in December 2025 and 117.8% in December 2024.

inflation_projection.sourceName: BCRA market expectations survey (REM): median expected inflation for the next 12 months 21.1% (September 2026)
inflation_projection.note: The central bank has no inflation target and the 5-year average is far above 50%, so we plan with 20%, near the market's 12-month expectation, which assumes disinflation continues; review yearly.

policy_rate.note: The BCRA stopped setting a monetary policy rate in July 2025 (last value 29% nominal on 10 July 2025, BCRA series 160) and now targets monetary aggregates; the overnight repo rate between third parties was 20.7% on 29 October 2026 (series 150).

savings_account_rate.sourceName: BCRA daily series of deposit interest rates (table IX-2-1-2-4-1, individuals' peso savings accounts)
savings_account_rate.note: Individuals' ordinary peso savings accounts paid 3.4-3.6% nominal a year for balances up to ARS 500,000 (3.1% for ARS 500,000-999,999); the all-depositor average was 4.6%.

fdr_3m_rate.sourceName: BCRA daily series of deposit interest rates (table IX-2-1-2-4-1, individuals' peso time deposits of 60 days and more)
fdr_3m_rate.note: Individuals' peso time deposits of 60 days or more paid 20.9-21.5% nominal a year (balances up to ARS 1 million); 30-day deposits system-wide 22.39% (BCRA series 12). No separate 90-day series is published.

fdr_1y_rate.note: The BCRA publishes deposit rates only up to the bucket '60 days and more' (about 21-23% nominal for individuals in October 2026); no 1-year time deposit average found.

dps_rate.note: No monthly recurring deposit product found in the BCRA deposit rate series for Argentina.

bank_deposit_avg_rate.sourceName: BCRA daily series of deposit interest rates (table IX-2-1-1, peso time deposits, all terms)
bank_deposit_avg_rate.note: Weighted average rate on new peso time deposits of all terms 23.13% nominal a year; peso savings accounts averaged 4.55%. World Bank FR.INR.DPST gives 34.9% for 2025.

sanchayapatra_5y_rate.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond sold directly to individuals found; Treasury securities are sold by auction and traded through brokers.

tbill_91d_rate.sourceName: Ministry of Economy, Secretariat of Finance: Treasury auction results of 28 October 2026
tbill_91d_rate.note: New fixed-rate capitalising Treasury letter (LECAP) maturing 26 February 2027 (about 4 months) cut at 2.10% a month effective, 28.32% effective annual yield (about 25.2% nominal). No 91-day letter was offered.

tbond_5y_rate.note: No 5-year fixed-rate peso bond yield found in official auction results; recent long peso issues are CER-linked (real yields about 6%) or TAMAR-linked.

tbond_10y_rate.note: No 10-year peso government bond is issued; recent official auctions go out to 2028.

tax_bank_interest.sourceName: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Argentina, individual income determination (last reviewed 16 June 2026)
tax_bank_interest.note: PwC: interest on savings accounts in Argentine banks is exempt from personal income tax, and the exemption for individuals' term deposits was extended to foreign-currency deposits from fiscal years starting 1 January 2026; other interest income is taxable at the progressive rates.

tax_sanchayapatra_profit.note: No government savings certificate for individuals exists; PwC notes capital gains on Argentine government bonds are exempt from income tax.

deposit_insurance_limit.sourceName: SEDESA (statutory deposit guarantee fund administrator): Deposit Guarantee System
deposit_insurance_limit.note: The deposit guarantee covers up to ARS 50,000,000 per person across accounts and deposits at a participating institution; joint accounts share one limit.

credit_card_rate_cap.sourceName: BCRA monthly series of lending rates to individuals (credit card system, total)
credit_card_rate_cap.note: Typical (weighted average) annual nominal rate on peso credit card balances of individuals 79.1% in September 2026; personal loans averaged 60.6% (October 2026).

equity_return_low.sourceName: BCRA: peso deposits 21-23%, LECAP 28% effective; peso depreciation about 58% a year 2016-2026 (BCRA series 5)
equity_return_low.note: Low case below deposit rates, reflecting the main index's very volatile record and periods of large losses in dollar terms.

equity_return_base.sourceName: BCRA: peso time deposits 21-23% (October 2026); LECAP 28.3% effective
equity_return_base.note: Base case only about 1-2 points above untaxed peso deposits, because the local index's 10-year record in dollar terms is weak and erratic; within 4 points of the safe rate.

equity_return_high.sourceName: BCRA wholesale exchange rate series 5; inflation expectation 21% (REM)
equity_return_high.note: High case: 20% inflation plus a strong real equity return of about 10%.

gold_return_low.sourceName: BCRA wholesale exchange rate (ARS 15.85 per USD end-2016, 1,537 on 30 October 2026)
gold_return_low.note: Low case: weak dollar gold and slower peso depreciation than inflation.

gold_return_base.sourceName: BCRA wholesale exchange rate series 5; REM inflation expectation 21%
gold_return_base.note: Dollar gold trend of about 4% plus peso depreciation of about 15% a year, close to the expected inflation gap with the US.

gold_return_high.note: High case: strong dollar gold and a faster peso slide.

fixed_income_return_low.sourceName: BCRA: individuals' 30-day peso time deposits about 19.7% nominal
fixed_income_return_low.note: Low case: rolling short peso deposits if rates keep falling with inflation.

fixed_income_return_base.sourceName: BCRA: individuals' peso time deposits of 60 days and more about 21%; interest on peso deposits largely untaxed
fixed_income_return_base.note: Base case at current 60-day-plus deposit rates.

fixed_income_return_high.sourceName: Treasury auction 28 October 2026: LECAP 28.3% effective annual
fixed_income_return_high.note: High case mixing short Treasury letters and deposits.

life_claim_settlement_rate.note: Searched the Superintendencia de Seguros de la Nación material: no industry-wide life claim settlement ratio published.

insurance_term_premium_table.note: Term life cover is sold in Argentina, but no regulator or other non-company source publishing premium rates by age was found.

health_hospitalisation_cost.note: No published typical cost of a major private hospital stay found for Argentina; public hospitals are free at the point of use.

health_premium_table.note: Private prepaid health plan prices are set by each company; no regulator table of premiums by age per 100,000 of cover found.

goal_inflation_health.sourceName: INDEC CPI via BCRA series 28; REM 12-month expectation 21.1%
goal_inflation_health.note: No long health CPI series was read, so we plan with the 20% projection plus two points, as private health plan fees have tended to rise faster than prices.

goal_inflation_education.sourceName: INDEC CPI via BCRA series 28 (education among the September 2026 leaders)
goal_inflation_education.note: Education led price rises in September 2026, so we plan with the 20% projection plus two points.

life_expectancy.note: UN WPP 2024 (via populationpyramid.net) gives 77.8 for 2026 (men 75.3, women 80.3).

life_table_remaining.sourceName: UN World Population Prospects 2024 via populationpyramid.net
life_table_remaining.note: Secondary source of UN WPP 2024 medium variant for 2026; totals at 60, 70 and 80 are the mean of men and women (only the 65 total is published there).

support_ratio.sourceName: World Bank SP.POP.DPND.OL (2025); UN WPP 2024 via populationpyramid.net (2040, 2065)
support_ratio.note: 100 / old-age dependency ratio: 19.0 (2025, World Bank), 23.7 (2040) and 43.3 (2065, populationpyramid.net/argentina/2065/).

retirement_age_default.sourceName: Law 24.241 (Integrated Pension System), article 19, consolidated text on InfoLEG
retirement_age_default.note: Men qualify for the basic universal pension at 65 and women at 60 (women may keep working to 65), with 30 years of contributions.

retirement_age_government.sourceName: Law 24.241 (Integrated Pension System), article 19, consolidated text on InfoLEG
retirement_age_government.note: National public employees are covered by the same SIPA rules (men 65, women 60); provinces and some professions run their own schemes with different ages.

retirement_return_low.sourceName: BCRA: individuals' 30-day peso deposits about 19.7% nominal
retirement_return_low.note: Low case if peso deposit rates keep falling.

retirement_return_base.sourceName: BCRA: individuals' peso time deposits of 60 days and more about 21%
retirement_return_base.note: Base case just below the current 60-day-plus deposit rate, untaxed for savings interest.

retirement_return_high.sourceName: Treasury auction 28 October 2026: LECAP 28.3% effective annual
retirement_return_high.note: High case mixing Treasury letters and deposits.

retirement_accumulation_return_low.sourceName: Mix of peso deposits (about 21%) and local equities
retirement_accumulation_return_low.note: Low case for a balanced peso mix in a bad decade.

retirement_accumulation_return_base.sourceName: Mix of peso deposits (about 21%) and equities (23% base)
retirement_accumulation_return_base.note: Base case for a roughly half-and-half mix, about 2 points above expected inflation.

retirement_accumulation_return_high.sourceName: Mix of Treasury letters (28% effective) and equities (32% high case)
retirement_accumulation_return_high.note: High case with strong equities and high peso yields.

old_age_allowance_monthly.note: The Universal Old-Age Pension (PUAM, Law 27.260) exists and pays 80% of the minimum retirement pension (argentina.gob.ar Derecho Fácil), but no official figure for the current minimum pension could be read: ANSES pages returned errors or empty content, and the only October 2026 figure found was a commercial news headline whose article did not state the minimum pension or the PUAM amount.

old_age_allowance_eligibility.sourceName: Ministry of Justice, Derecho Fácil: Pensión universal para el adulto mayor (Law 27.260)
old_age_allowance_eligibility.note: Non-contributory pension from 65 for citizens (naturalised after 10 years' residence, foreigners after 20); ANSES runs a socio-economic and asset assessment, and claimants must not receive or be entitled to any other pension. It rises with the minimum pension and includes PAMI health cover.

gratuity_rule.note: Argentina has no statutory gratuity on retirement or resignation: Labour Contract Law 20.744 art. 252 lets the employer end the contract once the worker is 70 and qualifies for the pension, without paying the seniority indemnity; the only statutory payment is the art. 245 dismissal indemnity of one month's best pay per year of service on dismissal without just cause (InfoLEG consolidated text, https://servicios.infoleg.gob.ar/infolegInternet/anexos/25000-29999/25552/texact.htm).

public_pension_scheme.sourceName: Law 24.241 (Integrated Pension System), articles 19 and 32, consolidated text on InfoLEG
public_pension_scheme.note: Compulsory pay-as-you-go SIPA run by ANSES: pension at 65 for men and 60 for women with 30 years of contributions; benefits are adjusted every month by the INDEC CPI since July 2024 (art. 32 as replaced by Decree 274/2024).

fdr_1y.note: Offered by banks, but the BCRA publishes no separate 1-year rate.

dps.note: No standard monthly recurring deposit product found.

sanchayapatra_5y.note: No government savings certificate or retail savings bond sold directly to individuals found.

tbill_91d.localName: Letra del Tesoro Nacional Capitalizable en pesos (LECAP)
tbill_91d.note: Short fixed-rate Treasury letters sold at fortnightly auctions and traded on the market; recent new issues run about 4 months.

tbond_5y.localName: Bono del Tesoro Nacional en pesos
tbond_5y.localNameEn: Peso Treasury bond (fixed-rate, CER-linked or TAMAR-linked)
tbond_5y.note: Peso bonds trade on the local market; no official 5-year fixed-rate yield found.

tbond_10y.note: No 10-year peso government bond is issued.

equity_fund.localName: Fondo común de inversión de renta variable
equity_fund.note: Mutual funds are regulated by the Comisión Nacional de Valores.

gold.note: Physical gold can be bought legally.

centralBank.name: Banco Central de la República Argentina (BCRA)

insuranceRegulator.name: Superintendencia de Seguros de la Nación (SSN)

insuranceComplaints.name: Superintendencia de Seguros de la Nación: consultas y denuncias

oldAgeAllowance.name: Pensión Universal para el Adulto Mayor (PUAM), paid by ANSES

publicHealthCover.name: Ministerio de Salud (free public hospitals; PAMI for retirees)

depositInsurance.name: Sistema de Seguro de Garantía de los Depósitos (administered by SEDESA)

statistics.name: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INDEC)
